title: Dynamic Social Democracy: An Alternate History
author: Autumn Chen, modded by munt

content.content: The Reichstag elections are to be held now.

content: Windelen opens negotiations with Alfred Dregger, Otto Graf Lambsdorff and Franz Schönhuber. The first dispute is over the
. Schönhuber asks for the Interior Ministry; the Christian Labour Association announces that it will oppose any coalition agreement which gives him a cabinet post.
A compromise leaves the
outside the cabinet but binds it to the government on confidence and supply. Dregger receives Interior for the
, while the
takes Finance. The
retains its separate parliamentary organisation.

Schönhuber accepts after the coalition agrees to introduce a new asylum bill before the summer recess. Several Christian Labour deputies abstain on the coalition agreement, but not on the investiture.

content.content: Heinrich Windelen is elected Chancellor. The People's Bloc has survived the election; the argument over what membership in it means has not.

content: Burkhard Hirsch agrees to talks once Windelen confirms that neither the
nor the
will enter the cabinet. The
wants the Silesian reprocessing project abandoned. The
insists that the replacement energy programme include the coal districts rather than simply closing them.
The smaller parties are not asked to join the cabinet. The
and
instead sign a toleration agreement covering the budget and confidence votes.
Dregger withdraws the
from the People's Bloc steering committee. Schönhuber follows and accuses Windelen of using NDPD voters to restore the old Weimar centre. Lambsdorff keeps the
in government.

content.content: Windelen is elected Chancellor. The new government has a majority, although neither electoral bloc leaves the negotiations intact.

content: Vogel initially rejects Windelen's approach. The
executive does not. With the Left Bloc unable to return to office and the alternative being a government dependent on Schönhuber, a majority votes to begin negotiations.
The
remains alongside the
, giving the arrangement a narrow majority. Vogel accepts the vice-chancellorship and Labour; the Silesian project is sent back to the states for review.
Lafontaine calls the agreement the final proof that the
was right to leave the Social Democrats. Hirsch is no more enthusiastic: the
has brought down one Vogel cabinet only to watch him enter another.

content.content: Windelen is elected Chancellor. The two largest parties are in government together for the first time in more than a decade.

options.title: Timeline of the Weimar Republic before 1928

content.content: The Reichstag elects the Chancellor and may remove a government only by electing a successor.
The President is directly elected. The office appoints the Chancellor, may dissolve the Reichstag, and retains limited emergency powers.
Seats are allocated proportionally within the states, with national adjustment seats.

library_timeline.title: Timeline of the Weimar Republic before 1928

content.content: TIMELINE OF THE SPD AND THE REPUBLIC (UNTIL 1928)

content: : The SPD is formed as a merger of the General German Workers' Association, founded by Ferdinand Lassalle, and the Social Democratic Workers' Party of Germany, led by Wilhelm Liebknecht and August Bebel.
: The Great War begins.
: The USPD, a left-wing anti-war split from the SPD, is formed.
: Following defeats in the war and uprisings by soldiers, sailors and workers, SPD leader Philipp Scheidemann proclaims the German Republic, and Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicates.
: The Spartacist uprising is defeated by the Social Democratic government.
: The Kapp Putsch is defeated by a general strike.
: Communist uprisings in Saxony and Hamburg are defeated.
: The Treaty of Rapallo normalises relations with the Soviet Union.
: Hyperinflation and the occupation of the Ruhr bring the Republic close to collapse.
: The Dawes settlement reduces the immediate reparations burden and opens a period of relative economic stability.
: Friedrich Ebert dies.
: A referendum on the expropriation of the former ruling houses fails.
: The SPD returns as the largest party.

Preferred Chancellor: Windelen 38%; Vogel 34%; Hirsch 9%; Lafontaine 7%; Dregger 5%; other or undecided 7%.
Silesia dominated the final fortnight. Employment remained the larger concern.
